_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909326.text: The Knicks (1-2 in the Cup) can still reach the knockout round, but only by beating Miami by at least seven and getting a Philadelphia loss at Indiana, so expect them to push to the final whistle. Miami are 2-1 with a +25 differential and already hold the first wild-card spot. New York's health is the worry: OG Anunoby (calf) is day-to-day after three missed games, and Jalen Brunson was questionable with an illness on Wednesday. The motivation edge leans New York; the injury list leans Miami.

401909327.text: Cade Cunningham was a late scratch on Tuesday with right-knee soreness, and J.B. Bickerstaff would only say he is 'battling through a lot'; he is day-to-day for Friday. Detroit showed they can cope, beating Orlando 104-86 without him behind 21 from Isaiah Joe. Milwaukee only just ended a 13-game losing streak. Even if Cunningham sits again, the spot leans Detroit.

401909328.text: Tyrese Haliburton practised on Wednesday after missing 14 straight games with a hamstring strain, and Rick Carlisle answered 'stay tuned' when asked about Friday. Indiana come in off a 125-120 win over Oklahoma City. Philadelphia (2-1) are playing for East Group B, while Joel Embiid has been out ill. A Haliburton return or another Embiid absence would tilt a near coin-flip towards Indiana; check the late injury report.

401909329.text: Kawhi Leonard (left-knee swelling) is out at least another week, with Dec 1 against Houston the earliest return. Toronto are also without RJ Barrett, and Brooklyn lost rookie Nolan Traore for 8-10 weeks. With both rosters thin, nothing in the news changes the numbers' lean towards Toronto at home.

401909330.text: This decides East Group C: Boston are 3-0 with a +68 differential, and Atlanta are 2-1 on a four-game winning streak, so both sides have plenty to play for. Jayson Tatum is rolling (41 against Washington on Tuesday). Atlanta are without CJ McCollum (calf), and Jock Landale (hip) is a game-time call. Motivation is even, so the lean stays slightly Boston at home.

401909332.text: Very little is at stake: Dallas clinched West Group A when Phoenix lost 116-104 to Houston on Wednesday, which also eliminated the Suns. The Mavericks are still without Dereck Lively II (foot). With nothing riding on the result for either side, watch for lighter minutes from Dallas's regulars. That leans slightly Phoenix at home.

401909333.text: The Lakers can advance with a win in their last Cup group game, and JJ Redick framed the moment bluntly: 'We're either going to be contenders or we're going to be a fake team.' Austin Reaves (heel) had his first full practice on Wednesday, and Friday is undecided. San Antonio's 12-game winning streak ended at Portland on Wednesday, and De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper are still out. The urgency leans Lakers, more so if Reaves plays.

401909336.text: Stephen Curry (oblique tear) is re-evaluated on Friday, but that is a checkpoint, not a return date, and he will need a ramp-up first. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are also out, and Golden State are 1-4 since Curry got hurt, with Draymond Green and Brandin Podziemski carrying more of the ball-handling. The news leans clearly Portland.
